# 30 THE DØG — voicing round (Batch 1A, the attack set)

*Generated by tests/voicing/batch01a.py. Level-matched to the bank reference (−18.0 dBFS RMS, note-on region) on phrase (e) LOW UNISON (A0-A2 roots held and chopped); the bank's own phrase (b) is in the table as well. Every parameter change is before → after under the echo rule in numbers.md.*

**Recommended: B centre** — the tight, punchy stack the brief asks for: 8 voices over 9.4 (step 1.3) cents by the DETUNE law (DETUNE 28; the original spread 8 voices over 78.1 (step 11.2)), 85% of the energy under 150 Hz (the drone this replaces: 97%, centroid 102 Hz vs 713 Hz now), the filter envelope opens each note (1224 Hz at the attack, 725 Hz in the body, +4.0 dB snap), it chops clean (62 ms to −60 dB) and peaks at -6.2 dBFS (worst-case CPU 1616 host instr/sample against the original's 2588). C is the same patch looser (snap +2.0 dB, more wander); D opens the filter and bites harder (centroid 1220 Hz).

## What to listen to

`*_lowuni.wav` is the one to judge (A1 held 3 s, A0 held, chopped roots, A2): weight, the width of the stack, the chop. `*_riff.wav`
is the pilot's low riff (A1-A2), `*_held.wav` / `*_stabs.wav` are there for the bank's own readings. Listen for: how fat versus how
punchy B is (the attack should snap, the body should be a wall), and whether C's looser stack is seasick or just fat.

*Notes.* The measured beat rate is the analysis window's floor (~0.4 Hz) and cannot tell B from C; the detune-law row is the real spread.
GROWL leaves a tiny constant DC offset behind after the note (the 10 Hz DC blocker's integer rounding, −44 … −53 dBFS, inaudible, an
engine trait left alone); release times are read after subtracting it. Variant A is rendered through the base firmware's own program path.
